answers.value: The completed referral record for each account escalated to Senior Underwriter / Chief Underwriter review under authority matrix v3.2 — referral rationale, recommendation, limits/appetite check, and the final authority decision with conditions. Scope = all closed referral files for the review queue in the current quarter across P&C commercial, life and specialty lines.
Referral files finalized in the current calendar quarter (e.g. Q2 2026, 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30); records outside the retention filing window are excluded from this batch.

Each retained record carries submission ID, insured name, line of business, referral trigger code, decision (accept/decline/conditional), authority level applied, and reviewer ID. A record missing decision, reviewer or authority level is rejected back to the underwriting file for completion before filing.

Count of referral records archived reconciles to the referral log in the GRC platform: (records closed in quarter) = (records filed to retention). Any delta between the referral queue and the archive is investigated; target variance = 0.

Referral record locked as an immutable PDF in OpenText under /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/ with version label v1 and system timestamp; retention set to 7 years per the state records-retention and market-conduct schedule.

Records that fail the completeness check are logged as an exception in the referral log with disposition (return-to-underwriter / waive-with-CUO-note) and a 2-business-day remediation SLA before the quarter's archive is certified complete.

Filing cites the company Underwriting File Documentation & Retention standard and the applicable state market-conduct records-retention requirement (typically 5-7 years post-expiration); citation recorded on the archive cover sheet.
Retention configured at 7 years from policy expiration in OpenText; legal-hold flag honored where the account is subject to litigation or a pending regulatory exam, suspending automatic purge.
Record filed to retention within 5 business days of the referral decision being finalized; late filings flagged on the monthly UW quality dashboard.
Monthly 5% sample of archived referral records (minimum 25 files) drawn by Underwriting Quality across all lines.

PASS = 100% of sampled records are complete, immutable, correctly indexed by submission ID, and within the 7-year retention setting. FAIL = any record missing the decision/authority fields, editable, mis-indexed, or purged early.

On FAIL, re-file the corrected record, log the gap in the GRC platform, and where a record was purged or lost escalate to the Chief Underwriting Officer within 24 hours for a documented recovery/root-cause note.
Acceptance = every finalized referral is retrievable within one business day for regulatory inspection, reinsurance audit or internal governance review, with a complete decision trail.
OpenText /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/ and the referral audit log in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC).

Field definitions from the referral-record data dictionary: submission_id, insured, line_of_business, referral_trigger, authority_level, decision, conditions, reviewer_id, decision_timestamp. Control total = count of referral records per line reconciled between the referral queue and the OpenText archive.

Applicable rule = state market-conduct records-retention requirement (5-7 years post-expiration) plus reinsurance treaty audit-access clauses; cited on the archive cover sheet with the internal File Documentation standard reference.

checklist.step: Assemble the complete referral file before archiving
checklist.value: Referral rationale, appetite/limit check, recommendation, decision and conditions all present in the record under /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/.

checklist.step: Index each record for retrieval
checklist.value: Record tagged by submission ID, insured, line of business and decision date so it is retrievable within one business day.

testing.step: Sample archived files for documentation completeness
testing.value: Monthly 5% sample (min 25 files); 100% contain the decision, authority level and reviewer sign-off; 0 incomplete.
Pull 5 random archived referrals on demand; all returned within one business day with full decision trail.

checklist.step: Apply the retention schedule to every referral record
checklist.value: OpenText retention set to 7 years from policy expiration; legal-hold flag suspends purge for litigated or examined accounts.

checklist.step: Prevent premature deletion
checklist.value: Records stored immutable (locked PDF, version v1); no delete permission granted to underwriting users.

testing.value: Sampled records show correct 7-year retention date and immutable flag; 0 editable or short-retention records.
For accounts under exam/litigation, retention date shows hold; 0 auto-purged.

checklist.step: Preserve the referral decision audit trail
checklist.value: Every state change (referred, reviewed, decided, filed) captured with actor and timestamp in the GRC referral log.

testing.value: For sampled referrals, the log shows an unbroken actor/timestamp chain from referral to archive; 0 gaps.

removeAppNames: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)

answers.value: Referred accounts approved on a conditional basis where additional information or a loss-control commitment is required before or after binding. Scope = all conditional approvals set during Senior Underwriter / Chief Underwriter review in the current period across commercial and specialty lines.
Current review cycle / month of decision (e.g. 2026-06); conditions are tracked from the approval date to their satisfaction deadline.

Each condition records: condition text, type (subjectivity / loss-control / documentation), owner, due date, and satisfaction status. A conditional approval with no due date or unassigned condition owner is invalid and returned to the underwriter.

Count of open conditions in the PAS subjectivities register reconciles to the referral decision log; every condition maps to exactly one approved referral. Delta between the two must be 0 at cycle close.

Conditions memorialized on the policy record in Guidewire PolicyCenter and the signed conditional-approval note archived to OpenText under /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/ with timestamp and version v1.

Conditions not satisfied by their due date are logged as an exception with disposition (extend / waive-with-CUO-approval / cancel-or-non-renew) and escalated to the Chief Underwriting Officer; 10-business-day cure SLA before re-escalation.
All conditional approvals in the current month plus any prior-period conditions still open (census, not a sample).

PASS = every conditional approval has clearly worded, dated, owned conditions recorded on the policy and tracked to closure. FAIL = any condition that is vague, undated, unowned, or bound without the required subjectivity recorded.
Unsatisfied conditions past due trigger a subjectivity-management workflow; unresolved cases route to the Chief Underwriting Officer for a waive/cancel decision documented in the referral log.
Acceptance = conditions are specific, measurable, dated and owned; recorded on the risk before coverage is confirmed; and closed with evidence when satisfied.
Guidewire PolicyCenter subjectivities/conditions register and OpenText /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/; tracking in the GRC platform.

Field definitions from the conditions register: condition_id, submission_id, condition_type, condition_text, owner, due_date, status, satisfied_date. Control total = open conditions reconciled between PolicyCenter and the referral decision log per line of business.

checklist.step: Record the conditional decision within 24 hours
checklist.value: Approval with conditions written to the policy record and referral log within 24 hours of the review decision.

testing.value: Sampled conditional approvals show decision-documented timestamp within 24h of review; 0 late.

checklist.step: Route any appetite/rate exception in the conditions to CUO
checklist.value: Conditions that involve deviation from filed rates or appetite carry a documented Chief Underwriting Officer approval before binding.

testing.value: Every conditional approval containing an exception has a linked CUO sign-off; 0 exceptions bound without it.

checklist.step: Document each condition on the file
checklist.value: Condition text, type, owner and due date recorded on the policy and in the archived approval note.

testing.value: Monthly sample; 100% of conditional approvals fully documented and tracked; 0 undocumented.

answers.value: Referred accounts where the reviewer challenges the referring underwriter's proposed pricing and terms against filed rates, the pricing tool output and portfolio loss-ratio targets. Scope = large/complex accounts in the Senior Underwriter / CUO review queue for the current period.
Current review cycle (e.g. 2026-06); the challenge and its resolution are documented before the quote is released to the broker.

The challenge note records: proposed rate vs Earnix technical/indicated rate, deviation %, schedule/experience credits applied, target vs projected loss ratio, and the referring underwriter's response. A challenge without the technical-rate comparison is incomplete.

Rate figures in the challenge reconcile to the Earnix pricing worksheet for the account; premium, exposure base and credits match the PAS quote. Any mismatch is resolved before the challenge is closed.
Challenge discussion, rate comparison and agreed outcome archived to OpenText under /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/ with timestamp and version; a summary note logged on the referral record.

Where the referring underwriter and reviewer cannot agree, the disagreement is logged with disposition and escalated to the Chief Underwriting Officer / Head of Pricing for adjudication; resolution recorded within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Compare proposed pricing against filed rates and the authority matrix
checklist.value: Challenge quantifies deviation % from filed/technical rate and confirms it is within the referring underwriter's authority per matrix v3.2 or requires escalation.

testing.value: Sampled challenged accounts show any rate deviation is within authority or has documented sign-off; 0 unauthorized deviations released.

checklist.step: Involve actuarial on large accounts
checklist.value: For accounts above the large-account threshold, the Pricing Actuary reviews rate adequacy as part of the challenge.

testing.value: Every challenged large account carries a Pricing Actuary rate-adequacy note; 0 missing.

checklist.step: Document the pricing rationale and challenge outcome
checklist.value: Rate comparison, credits, and agreed terms captured in the archived challenge note on the file.

testing.value: Monthly sample; 100% of challenges show a documented rationale and outcome; 0 undocumented.

answers.value: Risks whose premium, limit, aggregate exposure or appetite deviation exceeds Chief Underwriting Officer authority under matrix v3.2 and therefore must be escalated to the underwriting committee. Scope = all over-authority referrals in the current committee cycle.
Current underwriting-committee cycle (e.g. the June 2026 committee); escalations are compiled ahead of the scheduled committee date.

Each escalation records: submission ID, line of business, the specific authority threshold breached (premium/limit/aggregate/appetite), exposure figures, reason for support, and a CUO recommendation. An escalation without the breached-threshold value is returned for completion.

Escalated items on the committee agenda reconcile to the over-authority flags in the referral log; every referral flagged over-CUO-authority appears on the agenda. Delta must be 0 before the committee convenes.
Escalation pack and committee agenda item logged in the GRC platform and archived to OpenText under /underwriting/referrals/committee/<cycle>/ with timestamp and version v1.

Time-critical risks that cannot wait for the scheduled committee are handled via a documented out-of-cycle CUO+committee-chair sign-off, logged as an exception with rationale and ratified at the next committee.

checklist.step: Escalate to the next authority level with a recommendation
checklist.value: Each over-authority risk is packaged with a CUO recommendation and full exposure rationale for the underwriting committee.

testing.value: Every committee escalation includes a documented recommendation; 0 escalations submitted without one.

checklist.step: Confirm the breached authority threshold
checklist.value: Escalation states which premium/limit/aggregate/appetite threshold in matrix v3.2 is exceeded and by how much.

testing.value: Sampled escalations verified against the authority matrix; 100% correctly exceed CUO authority; 0 mis-routed items.

checklist.step: Document committee/CUO approval for the exception
checklist.value: Committee decision (or out-of-cycle CUO+chair approval) recorded with conditions before the risk is bound.

testing.value: No over-authority risk is bound without a recorded committee or out-of-cycle approval; 0 exceptions.

answers.value: The authority sign-off decision recorded for each referred account after Senior Underwriter / CUO review — the accept/decline/conditional decision, the authority level exercised, and any attached conditions. Scope = all referral decisions signed off in the current period.
Current review cycle / month of decision (e.g. 2026-06); each sign-off is timestamped at the moment the decision is recorded.

Sign-off record captures: submission ID, decision, authority level applied, signer identity and role, any conditions, and decision timestamp. A sign-off missing the signer's authority level or identity is invalid and cannot bind.
Every bound/declined referral has exactly one recorded authority sign-off; the count of sign-offs reconciles to the count of decided referrals in the log. Delta must be 0.

Decision written to the policy record in Guidewire PolicyCenter and the signed decision memorialized in the GRC referral log with timestamp and immutable version; conditions replicated to the subjectivities register.

Any decision made outside the signer's authority is logged as an exception, blocked from binding, and routed to the Chief Underwriting Officer for re-sign-off or committee escalation; disposition recorded.

checklist.step: Record the sign-off decision within 24 hours
checklist.value: Decision, authority level and conditions written to the policy and referral log within 24 hours of review.

testing.value: Sampled sign-offs show timestamp within 24h of the review; 0 late.

checklist.step: Confirm the signer holds the required authority
checklist.value: Sign-off validated against matrix v3.2 for the account's premium/limit/line before the decision can bind.

testing.value: 100% of recorded sign-offs are within the signer's authority; 0 bound outside authority.

checklist.step: Attach CUO approval for any exception in the decision
checklist.value: Decisions containing an appetite/rate exception carry a linked Chief Underwriting Officer approval and documented conditions.

testing.value: Every exception decision has a CUO approval on file; 0 unapproved exceptions bound.

answers.value: The referral submission package assessed against the documented portfolio appetite (line of business, geography, industry) and the authority/aggregate limits before a decision is made. Scope = all referral packages in the Senior Underwriter / CUO review queue for the current period.
Current review cycle (e.g. 2026-06); appetite and limit checks are run against the appetite statement and aggregate position in force at the time of review.

The assessment records: target-class match (yes/no), no-write-list check, geography/industry appetite fit, requested limit vs authority, and incremental aggregate/PML impact. A package cannot be dispositioned until the appetite and limit fields are populated.

Exposure and limit figures in the package reconcile to the aggregate exposure report; the added limit plus in-force aggregate is checked against the zone/line cap. Any figure that does not tie is corrected before decision.

Appetite/limit assessment recorded on the referral record and archived to OpenText under /underwriting/referrals/<submission-id>/ with timestamp; the appetite-fit result logged in the GRC referral log.

Packages outside appetite or over the aggregate limit are logged as an exception with disposition (decline / refer-up / seek-CUO-appetite-exception) and routed to the Chief Underwriting Officer; resolution recorded within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Check the package against the documented appetite
checklist.value: Line of business, geography and industry compared to the appetite statement and no-write list; target-class fit recorded.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show a completed appetite-fit check; 0 dispositioned without it.

checklist.step: Confirm the correct referral trigger applied
checklist.value: Package tagged with the referral-trigger code that sent it to review, validated against the documented trigger list.

testing.value: 100% of reviewed packages carry a valid referral trigger; 0 mis-triggered or un-coded referrals.

checklist.step: Assess requested limit against authority and aggregate
checklist.value: Requested limit checked against matrix v3.2 authority and the in-force aggregate/PML cap for the zone and line.

testing.value: Sampled packages show limit within authority/aggregate or escalated; 0 over-limit risks passed without escalation.
